assignment.title: Designing a rate limiter
assignment.instructions: Write a design document for a rate limiter that protects the public API of the practice service. Cover the algorithm, who is limited, what happens on failure, and how the pieces fit together.

sections.heading: Instructions
paragraphs: Submit your design document by Friday as a DOCX file.

sections.heading: Criteria
paragraphs: Chooses an algorithm and justifies the choice
Limits per user, keyed by user id
Says what happens when Redis is unavailable, and why that choice is acceptable

sections.heading: Goal
paragraphs: The public API should not be overwhelmed by one noisy client. This document describes a rate limiter that sits in front of the application servers and rejects requests from a client that has used up its allowance, replying with status 429 and a Retry-After header.

sections.heading: Algorithm
paragraphs: I chose a token bucket. Each bucket holds up to 60 tokens and refills at one token per second, and every request removes one token. I picked it over a fixed window because a fixed window lets a client send a double burst across a window boundary, and over a sliding log because the log needs memory for every request while a bucket needs only two numbers per key. The token bucket also allows a short burst, which suits clients that open a page and fire several requests at once.

sections.heading: Who is limited
paragraphs: Limits apply per user. The key is the user id taken from the verified session, so the Redis key looks like ratelimit:{user_id}. Two users on the same network never share a bucket, and one user on two devices shares one.

sections.heading: When Redis is unavailable
paragraphs: If Redis is unavailable the limiter fails open.

sections.heading: Architecture
paragraphs: The request path and the places where the limiter reads and updates its state are shown in Figure 1. Please see Figure 1 for the components.
